CHN.note: China is now counted on its own national statistics (260 TWh, 2024) rather than the IEA's 100 TWh. The two are not a disagreement about arithmetic — they are different universes. 260 TWh against the IEA's 31.9 GW of counted capacity implies a load factor of 0.93, which is physically impossible: nothing draws 93% of nameplate every hour of the year. So the Chinese figure must cover facilities the IEA's capacity count excludes, most likely telecom and 5G network rooms. Using it makes China's own number right and makes cross-country comparison looser.
